The smallest valid layer is a fixed raw-source closure computed inside the owner and required end to end; promotion, runtime-environment sealing, independent signing trust, and cold-owner repair remain separate transactions.

dialectic_sweep: Hashing only a clean authority checkout is simpler but permits a configured or reused owner to execute different ranker bytes; owner-emitted identity closes that contradiction.
Allowing caller-selected quality thresholds makes an A-grade label meaningless; policy inputs may strengthen but never weaken the fixed corpus, metric, and latency floors.

Source closure identity is necessary but cannot prove equal Torch, Transformers, SentenceTransformers, NumPy, Python, or backend builds; documentation and receipts therefore reject a reproducibility overclaim.

A callable pure gate is testable but not an operational RSI loop without an independent evaluator, deployed trust/revocation, a non-test consumer, promotion/canary/rollback authority, and verified outcome learning.
first_principles: Retrieval evidence is valid only when the measured corpus, generation, repository, configuration, ranker source, and executing owner identity are bound and independently checkable.
A-grade is an admission result, not a feature name; unavailable runtime, missing environment identity, missing trust, or missing caller keeps the system below A-grade.
RSI requires an authenticated propose-evaluate-promote-observe-rollback loop. Exact-generation repair RSI works, while retrieval-quality RSI does not yet exist operationally.
The thin VSIX remains a consumer of bounded read-only evidence and receives no Holo maintenance, reindex, repository, worker-dispatch, or promotion authority.
